roster.name: Mega Gengar
roster.rationale: Shadow Tag is uniquely matchup-warping, while Mega Gengar also provides elite Speed, immediate damage, Perish Song, Disable, Taunt, and broad control options.

roster.name: Maushold
roster.rationale: Unique Follow Me plus Friend Guard strongly enables Mega Gengar’s trapping, setup, and Perish endgames while adding Encore, Feint, Super Fang, and Helping Hand utility.

roster.name: Primarina
roster.rationale: Bulky Water/Fairy offense patches Gengar’s Dark and Ground matchups, adds flexible speed control and utility, and provides a second Perish Song user without forcing a dedicated trap mode.

roster.name: Tsareena
roster.rationale: Queenly Majesty protects Mega Gengar from Fake Out and Sucker Punch, while Tsareena adds crucial Grass pressure into rain and Rotom-Wash plus Helping Hand, Taunt, U-turn, and broad physical coverage.

roster.name: Mega Skarmory
roster.rationale: Elite value as a second Mega: supplies Steel typing, Tailwind, Taunt, Ground immunity, strong physical pressure, and matchup flexibility when Mega Gengar is less favorable.

roster.name: Arcanine
roster.rationale: Adds the roster’s most reliable available Intimidate support, Fire coverage, Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, Helping Hand, and strong role flexibility beside Mega Gengar.

roster.name: Raichu
roster.rationale: Lightning Rod protects Primarina and Mega Skarmory, while Fake Out, Nuzzle, Encore, Electroweb, Feint, and Volt Switch provide flexible support for Mega Gengar trapping without consuming the Mega slot.

roster.name: Diggersby
roster.rationale: Secures our best remaining physical Ground attacker and completes the planned 6+3+1 budget structure.

roster.name: Morpeko
roster.rationale: Fast Fake Out, Parting Shot, Quash, Snarl, and Dark pressure provide the flexible disruption our trapping core lacks while preserving 2 points for the final slot.

roster.name: Qwilfish
roster.rationale: Adds a cheap second Intimidate, Haze, Taunt, Thunder Wave, Icy Wind, Flip Turn, and Whirlpool support for Mega Gengar trapping modes.

roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Best VGC foundation. Intimidate pivot with Fake Out/Parting Shot, resists Mega Gengar's Ghost STAB, and fits any future team skeleton. Leaves 82 points for 9 more picks.

roster.name: Rotom-Wash
roster.rationale: Rotom-Wash covers multiple threats: counters rain (Pelipper/Basculegion) and sun (Mega Charizard Y), provides speed control, and its Levitate + Electric/Water typing pairs excellently with Incineroar's Intimidate pivoting. Leaves budget for 8 more picks.

roster.name: Mega Metagross
roster.rationale: Mega Metagross at 17 points is premium value — Tough Claws boosts its heavy contact moves, 145/150/110 bulk anchors the team, Steel/Psychic patches Incineroar's Fairy weakness and resists the Ghost/Dark that threaten Rotom-Wash. Its Ground resistance helps cover my team's shared Ground hole.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Fastest special attacker on the board (142 Spe), provides Dragon/Ghost coverage my team lacks, Infiltrator bypasses screens/Aurora Veil, and Thunder threatens the rain team forming. Pairs cleanly with Metagross's physical pressure and Incineroar's pivoting.

roster.name: Meowscarada
roster.rationale: Counters the rain core (Pelipper/Swampert/Basculegion) built by kimi-k3. Fast Grass/Dark with Protean gives flexibility, Flower Trick always crits through defensive boosts. Leaves 25 points for 5 remaining slots to fill Ground, Fairy, Fighting roles and add weather control (Hippowdon).

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Sylveon was too frail (KOed T2 both Week 1 games). Gholdengo (16) replaces it with Good as Gold status immunity, Recover, superior bulk, and great Steel/Ghost typing vs upcoming matchups (blocks Hatterene/Farigiraf Taunt, OHKOs Clefable, checks Floette). Pyroar(2) filler downgraded to Pikachu(1) with Lightning Rod + Fake Out/Nuzzle utility, offsetting the +1 cost from Gholdengo. Budget stays 100/100.

roster.name: Skarmory
roster.rationale: Skarmory at 3 provides Ground immunity via Flying type, Stealth Rock, Spikes, Tailwind, Roost, and superb physical bulk. Addresses my team's Ground weakness, adds hazard setting and speed control — all at a bargain 3 points.

roster.name: Golurk
roster.rationale: Golurk provides essential Ground coverage my roster lacks, adds Ghost STAB, sets Stealth Rock, and pairs well with Rotom-Wash's Levitate for Earthquake. At 4 cost it leaves 3 points for the final two picks (2+1).

roster.name: Absol
roster.rationale: Absol (1) + Mawile (2) fit my 3 remaining points. Absol brings 130 Atk with Justified synergy (Incineroar's Dark moves trigger +1 Atk), Sucker Punch priority, and Swords Dance. Mawile adds a second Intimidate source with the Steel/Fairy typing that checks Fighting/Dragon/Dark threats across the league. Together they patch my lack of Fighting-type coverage and add priority options.

roster.name: Pikachu
roster.rationale: Sylveon was too frail (KOed T2 both Week 1 games). Gholdengo (16) replaces it with Good as Gold status immunity, Recover, superior bulk, and great Steel/Ghost typing vs upcoming matchups (blocks Hatterene/Farigiraf Taunt, OHKOs Clefable, checks Floette). Pyroar(2) filler downgraded to Pikachu(1) with Lightning Rod + Fake Out/Nuzzle utility, offsetting the +1 cost from Gholdengo. Budget stays 100/100.

roster.name: Farigiraf
roster.rationale: Armor Tail is unique on board and hard-counters Fake Out/Prankster from Incineroar and other support while enabling Trick Room. Most centralizing doubles piece left after Gengar/Incineroar gone, enables cheap slow megas later and is scarce - won't survive to 14.

roster.name: Mega Chandelure
roster.rationale: Farigiraf needs Ghost immunity vs enemy Mega Gengar Shadow Tag + Trick Room synergy. Chandelure-Mega is both: Ghost (Shadow Tag immune), learns Trick Room, 175 SpA / 90 Spe Infiltrator, and at 9pts is the best discount Mega value on board. Solves ghost requirement while adding premium slow TR sweeper, keeping points balanced (9 avg) for remaining 8 picks.

roster.name: Gallade
roster.rationale: Hard TR 29-65 auto-wins 95-123 if TR up. Gholdengo 16 benched vs Fairy Aura+Kingambit (MakeItRain 20-36% vs Kingambit then OHKO by Kowtow, HH blocked by Good as Gold) - 16pt situational bench. Gallade 10 adds second Wide Guard (vs Heat Wave/Hyper Voice/EQ/Rock Slide/Dazzling/Muddy Water) + Trick Room backup + Sharpness/Justified Close Combat for Kingambit/Incineroar/Metagross-Mega/Kangaskhan, 80spe still slower than 95-123 meta so moves first under TR. Keeps Trevenant 3 Grass for W7 rain (Pelipper/Swampert-Mega) and both Megas. Cost 100-16+10=94 leaves 6pts flex for later windows, uses 1/6 swaps.

roster.name: Mega Camerupt
roster.rationale: Mega Camerupt is the best discounted TR abuser left (20 Spe, 145 SpA Sheer Force) - perfect slowest attacker under Farigiraf Trick Room, fixes Steel coverage for Gholdengo/Chandelure, and keeps budget at 10pts (avg 8.1 remaining) while giving mega flexibility with Chandelure-mega. Resists Intimidate as special attacker.

roster.name: Reuniclus
roster.rationale: Reuniclus is 8-point Trick Room setter/sweeper at 30 Speed with Magic Guard (Life Orb, Recover, 125 SpA) — gives Farigiraf a secondary TR setter for redundancy vs Taunt/KO and our first true slow special TR abuser to pair with physical Mega Camerupt/Mega Chandelure. Keeps 39 points for 5 picks (avg 7.8) and still lets us grab Rhyperior/Cofagrigus + Intimidate next.

roster.name: Hatterene
roster.rationale: Locks second Trick Room setter with Magic Bounce to protect Farigiraf and bounce Taunt/Encore from Whimsicott/Sableye. Base 29 Speed and 136 SpA is perfect TR sweeper and keeps budget for Rhyperior (9) + Hydrapple (6) + Staraptor (Intimidate+Tailwind 10) + Cofagrigus (5 Ghost) to hit 100.

roster.name: Rhyperior
roster.rationale: Rhyperior 9 is premium Slow TR attacker (115/140/130, 40 Spe) with Solid Rock+Lightning Rod, gives Rock coverage vs Char-Y/Talonflame/Volcarona/Gyarados that our Psychic/Ghost core can't hit, and Ground STAB vs Kingambit/Archaludon/Metagross. Most contested TR piece remaining for rain/sun teams. Keeps 21 pts for 3 slots to add Intimidate/Fake Out Scrafty 3 + Grass Hydrapple 6 + 12-pt finisher (Ceruledge/Azumarill).

roster.name: Wyrdeer
roster.rationale: Scrafty 3 gone - Wyrdeer 7 is the last cheap slow Intimidate+TR setter (65 Spe, Intimidate/Frisk/Sap Sipper) perfect Farigiraf Armor Tail lead. Secures Intimidate vs Garchomp/Kingambit/Sneasler physical spam where Ox and Kimi still have zero Intimidate and will snipe. At 7 leaves 14 for 2 to fix Wide Guard + Grass vs Pelipper rain and Whimsicott Tailwind, more urgent than Fake Out since Armor Tail already blocks enemy Fake Out for our TR.

roster.name: Araquanid
roster.rationale: TR-speed Wide Guard + Water Bubble. 42 Spe fits Farigiraf/Reuniclus/Hatterene/Camerupt/Rhyperior TR, covers Fire for Grass, resists Water vs Basculegion/Mega Swampert rain, halves Fire. Leaves 3pts for Trevenant (56 Spe Ghost/Grass TR/WoW/Horn Leech) for exact 14pt finish, giving Grass vs Water/Ground and Ghost trap immunity vs Mega Gengar.

roster.name: Trevenant
roster.rationale: Completes planned Araquanid 11 + Trevenant 3 =14 TR core: Trevenant is 56 Spe Ghost/Grass TR setter - gives Grass coverage vs rain Swampert/Basculegion/Pelipper (we had zero Grass types), third Ghost to escape Mega Gengar Shadow Tag (with Gholdengo/Mega Chandelure), Trick Room redundancy with Farigiraf/Reuniclus/Hatterene, and slow TR speed perfect for Camerupt 20/Reuniclus 30/Araquanid 42.

roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Drought is the most impactful weather ability remaining on the board — it enables sun for the entire team (one-turn Solar Beam, Fire-type boosts, Chlorophyll sweepers). CMY is also a premier special attacker (159 SpA, 115 SpD, 100 Spe) with a 72-move learnset covering every role. The opposing Mega Gengar pick confirms a high-powered special attacker meta, and CMY fits right in while adding sun control that counters rain-dependent builds. Taking the premium 20-cost pick at slot 4 maximizes value before other coaches claim the remaining 19-cost Pokémon.

roster.name: Mega Kangaskhan
roster.rationale: Week 1 loss to minimax-m3 exposed two critical weaknesses: Sneasler (19pts) was OHKO'd by Brave Bird priority both games — too fragile for its price. Salazzle (7pts) had ineffective Corrosion status spreading against Steel/Water types. Swapping to Mega Kangaskhan (15pts) provides Fake Out (turn-1 safety, delays opponent leads), Sucker Punch (priority to eliminate their priority users first), and Parental Bond bulk. Replacing Salazzle with Alcremie (4pts) adds crucial Fairy typing (resists Dragon/Dark/Fighting — prevalent in meta), Sweet Veil (team sleep prevention vs Hatterene/Trevenant/Morpeko Hypnosis), and Light Screen support. Resulting 93/100 roster retains sun offense (Charizard-Y+Venusaur), multi-form speed control (Noivern Tailwind+Focus Sash, Venusaur Chlorophyll, priority from Kangaskhan+Stunfisk), hazard control (Swampert/Stunfisk SR, Corviknight Defog, Starmie Spin), and defensive cores (Toxapex special wall, Corviknight physical wall). 4 swaps saved for later windows.

roster.name: Noivern
roster.rationale: Pick 20: Noivern (9 pts) — fastest non-Prankster Tailwind setter (123 Spd), critical speed control anchor for doubles. Flying/Dragon provides special coverage with 140 BP Boom Burst spread, Draco Meteor, sun-boosted Flamethrower. Complements Mega Charizard Y's Drought and Sneasler's physical Poison threat. Plan unchanged: target Corviknight (13) at pick 29 and Venusaur (13) at pick 36 to complete the 74-point core, then ~26 pts across 5 fillers.

roster.name: Corviknight
roster.rationale: Planned pick 29: Corviknight (13) — Steel/Flying pivot with Intimidate, Defog, U-turn. Walls Fairy/Dragon threats, complements Charizard Y sun core, Sneasler Poison/Fighting, and Noivern speed control. Only viable Steel pivot left at this price point; Mega Scizor (13) is a cheaper option but Corviknight's typing and utility better fill the Fairy/Dragon answer role. 39 pts remaining for 4 picks.

roster.name: Venusaur
roster.rationale: Venusaur (13) is still available and locks in the Drought/Chlorophyll sun core with Charizard Y. Chlorophyll doubles Speed (outspeed base 80 mons like Dragapult with max investment), Sleep Powder provides utility support, instant Solar Beam, and the Overgrow→Chlorophyll ability is the key synergy. After this pick, 26 pts remain for 5 fillers: plan is Toxapex (8) defensive pivot, Salazzle (7) fast Poison/Fire utility, Starmie (4) water support/spin, + two 1-2pt value mons to fill slots.

roster.name: Swampert
roster.rationale: Ground immunity is critical for Sneasler (4x weak to Ground); Water/Ground typing provides Fire resistance for Charizard-Y/Venusaur/Corviknight; brings Wide Guard, Yawn, Flip Turn, Stealth Rock for doubles utility; steals 6pts from a 26pt budget efficiently, leaving 20pts for 4 fillers. Salazzle, Toxapex, Forretress, Starmie plan confirmed viable via learnset checks.

roster.name: Alcremie
roster.rationale: Week 1 loss to minimax-m3 exposed two critical weaknesses: Sneasler (19pts) was OHKO'd by Brave Bird priority both games — too fragile for its price. Salazzle (7pts) had ineffective Corrosion status spreading against Steel/Water types. Swapping to Mega Kangaskhan (15pts) provides Fake Out (turn-1 safety, delays opponent leads), Sucker Punch (priority to eliminate their priority users first), and Parental Bond bulk. Replacing Salazzle with Alcremie (4pts) adds crucial Fairy typing (resists Dragon/Dark/Fighting — prevalent in meta), Sweet Veil (team sleep prevention vs Hatterene/Trevenant/Morpeko Hypnosis), and Light Screen support. Resulting 93/100 roster retains sun offense (Charizard-Y+Venusaur), multi-form speed control (Noivern Tailwind+Focus Sash, Venusaur Chlorophyll, priority from Kangaskhan+Stunfisk), hazard control (Swampert/Stunfisk SR, Corviknight Defog, Starmie Spin), and defensive cores (Toxapex special wall, Corviknight physical wall). 4 swaps saved for later windows.

roster.name: Toxapex
roster.rationale: Toxapex fills the critical special wall gap on my roster. At 152/142 bulk with Regenerator and access to Scald/Recover/Toxic Spikes, it checks the many special attackers across the meta (Gholdengo, Mega Chandelure, Volcarona, Dragapult, Hydreigon) while synergizing with Salazzle's Corrosion status-spreading strategy. Forretress (my planned pick 68) was drafted by team7, so Starmie provides Rapid Spin instead and Absol (1) fills the priority gap with Sucker Punch — a net improvement for the same 13-point budget.

roster.name: Starmie
roster.rationale: Securing Starmie (4) before coach 7 (4pts) can contest it at pick 74. Heavy-Duty Boots is not legal in this format, making Rapid Spin + Defog combo even more critical for hazard control. Starmie provides 115 Speed, Natural Cure, Rapid Spin (also +1 Speed), and excellent coverage (Ice Beam for Dragon/Rock, Thunderbolt, Psychic/Psyshock). Replacing Absol (drafted by coach 2) with Stunfisk-Galar (1) as my final pick — Stunfisk-Galar learns Sucker Punch (priority I originally planned from Absol), sets Stealth Rock (more impactful without Heavy-Duty Boots), and provides crucial Fairy/Dragon/Ice resistance through Ground/Steel typing. Final roster: Charizard-Y (sun setter), Sneasler (Unburden sweeper), Noivern (Tailwind), Corviknight (Intimidate+Defog), Venusaur (Chlorophyll), Swampert (Ground immunity), Salazzle (Corrosion), Toxapex (special wall), Starmie (utility+Rapid Spin), Stunfisk-Galar (Stealth Rock+Sucker Punch).

roster.name: Galarian Stunfisk
roster.rationale: 1 point remaining, 1-cost Stunfisk-Galar provides Stealth Rock hazard setup (valuable without Heavy-Duty Boots), Sucker Punch priority for revenge killing, and Ground/Steel typing that resists Fairy/Dragon/Ice and is immune to Electric. Complements the sun core (Charizard-Y + Venusaur) and defensive core (Toxapex + Corviknight). Exactly as planned in my private draft note.

roster.name: Archaludon
roster.rationale: Top remaining foundational pick at 19. Steel/Dragon typing gives elite resistances, 130 Def + Stamina makes it snowball, Stalwart ignores redirection, and 125 SpA / 105 Atk with 85 Spe let it run either an offensive or tank set. After the four picks ahead (Mega Gengar, Incineroar, Farigiraf, Mega Char Y) removed Shadow Tag, Intimidate, Armor Tail, and Sun support, Archaludon is the safest anchor for any team archetype I might pivot to (rain, tailwind, trick room, or balanced) without locking me in early. Saving the 17–18 slot for pick 12 where I can react to the board.

roster.name: Talonflame
roster.rationale: Archaludon is slow and needs Tailwind support. Talonflame's Gale Wings gives priority Tailwind + priority Brave Bird, plus U-turn pivoting, Defog, and WoW — a perfect support/utility piece to complement my steel-dragon core. Leaves 66 points for 8 picks, keeping budget flexible for Sneasler/Sinistcha/Aero later.

roster.name: Clefable
roster.rationale: Clefable fills the critical Magic Guard status-immunity + Follow Me redirection niche my roster lacks. With Archaludon (slow Steel/Dragon weak to Fighting/Ground, often burned or statused) and Talonflame (Fast but frail Fire/Flying weak to Rock/Water/Electric), I need a bulky pivot that can absorb status, redirect opposing Dragon/Rock/Ice attacks away from my cores, and clean late with Moonblast. Unaware also handles opposing setup sweepers. Leaves 51 points / 7 picks (avg ~7.3) — plenty of room to grab a TR setter, ground-immunity pivot, and fast attacker in later rounds.

roster.name: Mega Delphox
roster.rationale: Best fit for my current core (Archaludon/Talonflame/Clefable). Mega Delphox provides a fast special attacker (134 Spe, 159 SpA) which I lack — Talonflame is physical, Archaludon is bulkier, and Clefable is support. Levitate gives Ground immunity, giving my team a safe pivot that absorbs Ground moves aimed at Archaludon's 4x weakness. Fire/Psychic STAB coverage complements the existing types well. Leaves 34 points across 6 remaining picks, which fits a balanced budget (e.g., 11+8+5+4+3+3 or similar).

roster.name: Excadrill
roster.rationale: Best available Rock-resist pivot (Talonflame 4x weak), immune to Poison (Clefable weakness), and Electric/Ground immunity. Sand Rush with cheap Hippowdon (5) gives outspeed (194+ eff Speed). Mold Breaker bypasses Levitate on Rotom-Wash and Sturdy mirrors. 13 pts leaves clean budget: Hippowdon(5)+Empoleon(7)+Conkeldurr(7)+2×1-pt fillers = 20 pts for remaining 5 picks.

roster.name: Hippowdon
roster.rationale: Lock in the sand setter now — only 5pts and the linchpin of my Excadrill Sand Rush strategy. Without it Excadrill is a slow pivot instead of a top-speed wallbreaker. Hippowdon also adds Intimidate + Ground/electric immunity coverage my team needs (Talonflame/Clefable weakness compression). Budget after: 16pts for 4 picks, still fits Empoleon (7) + Conkeldurr (7) + 2x1pt fillers.

roster.name: Empoleon
roster.rationale: Top-tier Steel/Water pivot still available at 7pts. Covers multiple team weaknesses: Clefable's 4x Ground weakness, Excadrill's Fire weakness, and adds Fire/Dragon/Ground resistances. Perfect team synergy piece for 7pts and gives me 9 left for Conkeldurr + fillers.

roster.name: Conkeldurr
roster.rationale: Best Fighting-type value left at 7 pts. Conkeldurr brings Drain Punch (healing), Mach Punch (priority that loves my sand from Hippowdon), Strength Sap (utility/healing), and Knock Off (item removal). Completes my physical wallbreaker slot to pair with the special attackers (Mega Delphox, Archaludon, Empoleon). Knocks out Dragons/Darks/Normals common across this league. Saves 2 pts for two 1-pt fillers next: Avalugg (Stealth Rock + physical wall) and Houndoom (Dark/Fire coverage with Flash Fire immunity for my Fire weakness).

roster.name: Forretress
roster.rationale: Avalugg(1) is a dead-weight bench piece — sand-boosted wall that only works under Hippowdon lead, niche. Forretress(1) adds Stealth Rock hazard control which was a confirmed gap in W1 (rocks never went up, cost flexibility on switch-ins). Sturdy gives a free turn to set hazards. Bug/Steel typing adds defensive value. Equal-priced 1-for-1 keeps both rosters at 100/100 with no species conflicts. Entrant 6 gets an Ice-type that pressures Dragons — directly useful against the metagame's Dragon-heavy builds and synergizes with their existing offense (Whimsicott Tailwind support).

roster.name: Stunfisk
roster.rationale: Stealth Rock + Volt Switch pivot + Electric immunity + Static spread + Sand Veil evasion combo with Hippowdon. 1-point utility that fills the hazard-control gap (Forretress taken) and gives team an Electric immunity pivot. Better than Houndoom (too frail) and Stunfisk-Galar (loses Static/Sand Veil).

roster.name: Mega Floette
roster.rationale: Mega Floette offers unmatched immediate special Fairy output with 155 SpA and Fairy Aura boosting Light of Ruin and Dazzling Gleam at a great 102 base Speed tier, serving as a premier win condition and wallbreaker.

roster.name: Kingambit
roster.rationale: Kingambit provides elite physical Steel/Dark presence to synergize with Mega Floette, offering Defiant to punish opposing Intimidate (Incineroar) and strong Sucker Punch priority against fast threats like Mega Gengar.

roster.name: Volcarona
roster.rationale: Volcarona provides crucial Fire-type offense, Rage Powder redirection to protect Kingambit and Mega Floette, Tailwind speed control, and a 4x Fighting resistance with Flame Body deterrence against Kingambit's primary weakness.

roster.name: Gyarados
roster.rationale: Gyarados provides Intimidate, Ground immunity, and key resistances (Water, Fire, Fighting, Steel) to seamlessly complement Kingambit and Volcarona while offering reliable speed control and Taunt utility.

roster.name: Gliscor
roster.rationale: Gliscor provides essential Electric immunity, Ground STAB, Tailwind speed control, and utility (Knock Off, U-turn, Feint) for just 3 points, preserving 35 points across our final 5 picks.

roster.name: Sinistcha
roster.rationale: Sinistcha provides elite redirection (Rage Powder), burst healing on entry via Hospitality, spread burn pressure with Matcha Gotcha, and crucial Trick Room speed control. It pairs exceptionally with Volcarona setup and Kingambit/Mega Floette positioning while locking down a crucial Grass/Ghost defensive profile against opposing rain and ground cores.

roster.name: Scrafty
roster.rationale: Scrafty provides invaluable Fake Out, Intimidate, Knock Off, Quick Guard, and pivot utility for just 3 points, pairing exceptionally well with Sinistcha Hospitality healing and our setup sweepers while leaving 14 points for our final 3 picks.

roster.name: Alolan Raichu
roster.rationale: Alolan Raichu provides essential high-speed utility (base 110 Speed) with Fake Out, Nuzzle, Electroweb, Encore, and Volt Switch, enabling free turns and positioning for Mega Floette and Volcarona while covering Water and Flying threats.

roster.name: Hisuian Goodra
roster.rationale: Hisuian Goodra gives the team an elite 80/100/150 defensive Steel/Dragon pivot with Sap Sipper/Shell Armor, providing a massive special wall, Dragon typing, and key resistances to complement Volcarona, Floette-Mega, and Gyarados while preserving 3 points for the final pick.

roster.name: Altaria
roster.rationale: Altaria provides invaluable defensive utility for only 1 point: Cloud Nine acts as a hard counter to heavy weather archetypes (both Laguna's Sun and Kimi's Rain), while its support movepool features Tailwind, Haze, Will-O-Wisp, Helping Hand, and Perish Song.

roster.name: Whimsicott
roster.rationale: Prankster support is the scarcest resource on this board and Whimsicott is the best of it: priority Tailwind, Encore, Taunt, Moonblast, and Grass/Fairy typing that checks the many Water/Ground/Dragon threats being drafted. Every strong doubles core wants this piece, and it slots into any archetype I end up building (Tailwind offense, sun, or balance).

roster.name: Garchomp
roster.rationale: Sticking to plan: Garchomp is the premier physical breaker left on the board and fills my speed tier + Ground coverage needs against already-drafted threats (Mega Charizard Y's Flying/Fire, Archaludon, Incineroar). Rough Skin/Sand Veil gives it defensive utility in doubles, and 102 Speed pairs naturally with Whimsicott's Tailwind or Encore support. Taking it now before another coach grabs the top-end physical slot.

roster.name: Mega Dragonite
roster.rationale: Primarina is gone, and the premium pivot alternatives (Milotic 14, Slowbro 7, Florges 7) are replaceable later — Mega Dragonite is not. It's the best remaining piece: Multiscale on a Mega, 145 SpA / 124 Atk mixed breaking with 115/125/100 bulk and base 100 Speed that Whimsicott's Tailwind makes fast. Fills my roster's total lack of a special attacker and gives a second win condition alongside Garchomp. I'm not spending this pick denying Kimi's rain a Mega Swampert — it doesn't fit my team without Drizzle.

roster.name: Milotic
roster.rationale: Priority 1 from my plan is intact: Milotic (14) is still on board, unclaimed by any of the seven rosters drafted so far. It fills my biggest structural gap — a bulky special pivot and Water answer — without overlapping Whimsicott/Garchomp/Mega Dragonite. Competitive punishes Intimidate cores (Incineroar, Krookodile users) that would otherwise wall my physical breakers, and Marvel Scale gives it longevity next to Tailwind support. Taking it now beats waiting because Kimi picks twice immediately (picks 27–28) and a bulky Water pivot fits either their rain build or a generic team.

roster.name: Mega Blaziken
roster.rationale: Mega Blaziken (12) is still on the board and was my top remaining priority: Speed Boost gives a self-sufficient breaker that doesn't conflict with Whimsicott's Tailwind or anyone's weather, pairs with Garchomp/Mega Dragonite as a third physical threat, and no rival coach has shown Fire/Fighting interest. This keeps my budget on track (12 spent here, 22 left for 5 picks) for Tinkaton (11) next, then Slowbro/Slowking + late-value fills.

roster.name: Tinkaton
roster.rationale: Tinkaton (11) was priority #1 in my plan and is still on the board. Steel/Fairy typing patches Garchomp/Mega Dragonite's shared Dragon/Fairy/Ice weaknesses, and Mold Breaker gives tech vs opposing Gholdengo/Clefable/Unaware walls. Mimikyu remains as fallback for later.

roster.name: Banette
roster.rationale: Original plan (Hydrapple at 6) is unaffordable without also cutting Houndstone, which forces 4 adds within 11 pts and filler depth. Now: cut dead weight Rotom/Furfrou/Avalugg (never contributed, Rotom explicitly useless vs meta) for three 1-pt functional bodies: Appletun (1-pt Grass/Dragon Water/Electric-resist insurance vs Kimi rain wk5), Chimecho (Levitate support/TR), Banette (Frisk/Destiny Bond utility). Roster 98/100, core six intact, Houndstone kept as Ghost depth; banked 3 swaps + 2 cap for window 2.

Drought is the most impactful weather ability remaining on the board — it enables sun for the entire team (one-turn Solar Beam, Fire-type boosts, Chlorophyll sweepers). CMY is also a premier special attacker (159 SpA, 115 SpD, 100 Spe) with a 72-move learnset covering every role. The opposing Mega Gengar pick confirms a high-powered special attacker meta, and CMY fits right in while adding sun control that counters rain-dependent builds. Taking the premium 20-cost pick at slot 4 maximizes value before other coaches claim the remaining 19-cost Pokémon.

Top remaining foundational pick at 19. Steel/Dragon typing gives elite resistances, 130 Def + Stamina makes it snowball, Stalwart ignores redirection, and 125 SpA / 105 Atk with 85 Spe let it run either an offensive or tank set. After the four picks ahead (Mega Gengar, Incineroar, Farigiraf, Mega Char Y) removed Shadow Tag, Intimidate, Armor Tail, and Sun support, Archaludon is the safest anchor for any team archetype I might pivot to (rain, tailwind, trick room, or balanced) without locking me in early. Saving the 17–18 slot for pick 12 where I can react to the board.

Mega Floette offers unmatched immediate special Fairy output with 155 SpA and Fairy Aura boosting Light of Ruin and Dazzling Gleam at a great 102 base Speed tier, serving as a premier win condition and wallbreaker.

Prankster support is the scarcest resource on this board and Whimsicott is the best of it: priority Tailwind, Encore, Taunt, Moonblast, and Grass/Fairy typing that checks the many Water/Ground/Dragon threats being drafted. Every strong doubles core wants this piece, and it slots into any archetype I end up building (Tailwind offense, sun, or balance).

Archaludon is slow and needs Tailwind support. Talonflame's Gale Wings gives priority Tailwind + priority Brave Bird, plus U-turn pivoting, Defog, and WoW — a perfect support/utility piece to complement my steel-dragon core. Sneasler (19) is the best available physical attacker with 130 Atk / 120 Spe. Poison typing provides crucial anti-Fairy tech against the meta's Fairy-heavy field (Floette-Mega, Whimsicoll drafted by other coaches). Poison Touch gives 30% poison chance on contact moves like Close Combat and Gunk Shot, devastating Fairy switch-ins that are everywhere. Fighting coverage handles Kingambit (Dark/Steel), Incineroar (Fire/Dark), and Rock/Steel types. Must secure at pick 13 before R3 coaches (picks 17-19) potentially take it. Completes physical/special attacker core with Mega Charizard Y (Drought sun special), while Sneasler can use Unburden/Poison Touch for speed or status hax. Remaining picks target: Noivern (9) for Tailwind speed control, Corviknight (13) for Steel pivot + U-turn, Venusaur (13) Chlorophyll sun sweeper, leaving 26 points for 5 fillers.

Farigiraf needs Ghost immunity vs enemy Mega Gengar Shadow Tag + Trick Room synergy. Chandelure-Mega is both: Ghost (Shadow Tag immune), learns Trick Room, 175 SpA / 90 Spe Infiltrator, and at 9pts is the best discount Mega value on board. Solves ghost requirement while adding premium slow TR sweeper, keeping points balanced (9 avg) for remaining 8 picks.

Rotom-Wash covers multiple threats: counters rain (Pelipper/Basculegion) and sun (Mega Charizard Y), provides speed control, and its Levitate + Electric/Water typing pairs excellently with Incineroar's Intimidate pivoting. Leaves budget for 8 more picks.
Unique Follow Me plus Friend Guard strongly enables Mega Gengar’s trapping, setup, and Perish endgames while adding Encore, Feint, Super Fang, and Helping Hand utility.
Bulky Water/Fairy offense patches Gengar’s Dark and Ground matchups, adds flexible speed control and utility, and provides a second Perish Song user without forcing a dedicated trap mode.

Mega Metagross at 17 points is premium value — Tough Claws boosts its heavy contact moves, 145/150/110 bulk anchors the team, Steel/Psychic patches Incineroar's Fairy weakness and resists the Ghost/Dark that threaten Rotom-Wash. Its Ground resistance helps cover my team's shared Ground hole.

16pt Steel/Ghost blocks Shadow Tag (Gengar-Mega already drafted) and Good as Gold protects TR plan. Complements Farigiraf (Armor Tail) + Mega Chandelure: two ghosts guarantee pivot vs trap, adds Steel resist and spread Make It Rain/Nasty Plot threat. Best-cost ghost on board – take before it goes, still leaves 57 for 7 (avg ~8.1) for cheap slow megas/TR abusers per plan.

Pick 20: Noivern (9 pts) — fastest non-Prankster Tailwind setter (123 Spd), critical speed control anchor for doubles. Plan unchanged: target Corviknight (13) at pick 29 and Venusaur (13) at pick 36 to complete the 74-point core, then ~26 pts across 5 fillers.

Clefable fills the critical Magic Guard status-immunity + Follow Me redirection niche my roster lacks. With Archaludon (slow Steel/Dragon weak to Fighting/Ground, often burned or statused) and Talonflame (Fast but frail Fire/Flying weak to Rock/Water/Electric), I need a bulky pivot that can absorb status, redirect opposing Dragon/Rock/Ice attacks away from my cores, and clean late with Moonblast. Unaware also handles opposing setup sweepers. Leaves 51 points / 7 picks (avg ~7.3) — plenty of room to grab a TR setter, ground-immunity pivot, and fast attacker in later rounds.

Volcarona provides crucial Fire-type offense, Rage Powder redirection to protect Kingambit and Mega Floette, Tailwind speed control, and a 4x Fighting resistance with Flame Body deterrence against Kingambit's primary weakness.

Fills my roster's total lack of a special attacker and gives a second win condition alongside Garchomp. I'm not spending this pick denying Kimi's rain a Mega Swampert — it doesn't fit my team without Drizzle.

Lightning Rod protects Primarina and Mega Skarmory, while Fake Out, Nuzzle, Encore, Electroweb, Feint, and Volt Switch provide flexible support for Mega Gengar trapping without consuming the Mega slot.

builds.rationale: Use Tsareena and Lightning Rod Raichu to deny priority and Electric pressure while Primarina supplies a reliable rain-resistant attacker with Energy Ball for Mega Swampert. Mega Gengar traps slower board states for direct KOs or Perish Song endgames, with Friend Guard Maushold providing redirection and disruption. Choice Scarf Diggersby pressures Aegislash and the opponent's Electric types while giving the team an Electric immunity.

Their roster orbits Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag and Mega Skarmory, with Primarina/Tsareena pressuring my Water-Ground core and Swift Swim Qwilfish trying to steal my rain. I run the Pelipper + Mega Swampert rain engine (Swampert hits 224 Speed in rain, outspeeding even Mega Gengar), with Heliolisk as the rain abuser whose 100%-accurate Thunder deletes Primarina, Qwilfish, and Skarmory-Mega (Electric is 2x into Steel/Flying) while Dry Skin heals off the weather. Hydreigon is my Gengar answer (Life Orb Dark Pulse OHKOs most spreads) and doubles as Skarmory/Tsareena pressure via Heat Wave; Levitate dodges Diggersby/Raichu ground-electric synergy. Aegislash is immune to Shadow Tag, survives Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball (58-98%) behind 167/162 bulk, and brings Wide Guard against Hyper Voice/Rock Slide spreads. Klefki gives Prankster Thunder Wave to neuter Gengar/Raichu/Skarmory-Mega speed and Light Clay screens, with Foul Play punishing Skarmory-Mega and Tsareena's big Attack stats. Bring 4 flexes by matchup: rain pair + Heliolisk vs their Waters/Skarmory, Hydreigon/Aegislash vs Gengar shells, Klefki whenever speed control matters.

This team answers the opponent's wide range of threats with a balanced offensive core and strong utility. Incineroar provides Intimidate pivoting and Fake Out pressure to nerf physical attackers like Mega Blaziken and Garchomp. Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice threatens Mega Dragonite and Garchomp with spread Fairy damage, and Life Orb pushes it past Multiscale rolls. Rotom-Wash handles Mega Blaziken (Hydro Pump), Milotic (Thunderbolt), and spreads burns. Metagross-Mega outspeeds and OHKOs Whimsicott with Meteor Mash, melts Garchomp with Ice Punch, and breaks screens with Psychic Fangs. Dragapult outspeeds everything, uses Dragon Darts to break Multiscale, and pivots with U-turn. Meowscarada's Flower Trick rips Milotic and Garchomp, Knock Off removes items, and Sucker Punch gives priority. Focus Sash keeps it alive to answer key threats.

They lean fast-offense around Mega Metagross, Dragapult, and Protean Meowscarada with Incineroar Intimidate support, so I'm leading my standard Tailwind core to flip the speed tiers immediately — Timid Whimsicott at 184 already outspeeds max Dragapult before Tailwind. Garchomp (148 Adamant) and Mega Dragonite punish the Steel/Psychic mega with Earthquake while Iron Head/Dragon Claw cover Sylveon and the dragons; Multiscale guarantees Dragonite gets a Dragon Dance off. Milotic's Competitive turns their Intimidate into a special-attack boost and its bulk plus Icy Wind handles Pyroar/Golurk while slowing the fast threats. Blaziken-Mega cleans late with Speed Boost and Thunder Punch specifically for Rotom-Wash, and Tinkaton provides Fake Out disruption, Thunder Wave for Dragapult/Meowscarada, and resists Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice.

Opponent leans on fast Fairy Aura Floette-Mega, Volcarona and Gliscor/Raichu spread damage plus Kingambit/Scrafty priority Fake Out/Sucker Punch. Farigiraf Armor Tail + Hatterene Magic Bounce give two Trick Room setters that block priority and Taunt, letting us reverse speed (29-55 base vs 95-110). Under TR Camerupt-Mega Sheer Force and Rhyperior OHKO Kingambit/Volcarona/Sinistcha/Gyarados, Araquanid Wide Guard blanks Heat Wave/Dazzling Gleam/Rock Slide/Discharge while Water Bubble Liquidation punishes Gliscor/Volcarona, and Gholdengo Good as Gold blocks status and nukes Floette with Make It Rain/Flash Cannon.

The opponent's roster leans heavily into Trick Room archetypes featuring slow powerhouses like Mega Camerupt, Rhyperior, and Araquanid supported by setters like Farigiraf, Reuniclus, and Hatterene alongside fast Ghost/Steel threats in Mega Chandelure and Gholdengo. We answer this with Sinistcha to reverse or deny Trick Room with Imprison while threatening Rhyperior and Camerupt with Matcha Gotcha, Kingambit to decimate their Psychic- and Ghost-heavy core with STAB Dark attacks, and dual Intimidate from Gyarados and Scrafty to neuter physical threats. Mega Floette and Hisuian Goodra provide high-impact special offense and defensive pivoting to punish their Fire, Ground, and Fairy coverage.

Against an opponent likely running a sand core with Mega Delphox, Excadrill, and Clefable, this team leverages Charizard-Y's Drought to set sun and pressure Fairy threats with boosted Fire STAB while Sneasler provides explosive physical damage via Unburden + White Herb. Noivern's Tailwind grants speed control to outpace faster threats like Mega Delphox, Corviknight provides Defog and physical bulk with Light Screen support, Toxapex walls special attacks while spreading Toxic Spikes for Venoshock double damage, and Stunfisk-Galar sets Stealth Rock and checks Fairy types with Ground/Steel typing plus Sucker Punch priority.

The opponent runs heavy special attackers (Mega Charizard Y, Noivern, Salazzle, Starmie) with key physical threats Sneasler and Corviknight. I build around a sand core: Hippowdon sets Sand Stream to enable Excadrill's Sand Rush sweep while tanking physical hits, Excadrill's Rock Slide hits Mega Charizard Y 4x SE with spread damage in doubles. Mega Delphox's 159 SpA with Levitate covers most special threats. Talonflame's Gale Wings priority Brave Bird handles revenge kills and Flare Blitz hits Sneasler/Venusaur 4x SE. Clefable's Magic Guard + Follow Me redirection + Moonblast for Dragon coverage rounds out support, and Conkeldurr's Iron Fist Drain Punch walls physical threats with sustain while Mach Punch gives priority.

decisions.rationale: Raichu and Primarina provide the safest rain lead: Fake Out pressures Pelipper while Energy Ball threatens Mega Swampert, and Lightning Rod denies Heliolisk. Tsareena supplies a second Swampert answer and blocks Prankster disruption, while Mega Gengar offers fast cleanup and trapping.

Lead Pelipper + Hydreigon: Drizzle sets rain immediately while Hydreigon pressures their Mega Gengar (Dark Pulse OHKO range) and Tsareena (Heat Wave), dodging Raichu/Diggersby synergies via Levitate. Swampert in back Mega Evolves into Swift Swim (outspeeds even Mega Gengar in rain) as the mid-game cleaner, and Heliolisk closes games against Primarina with rain-boosted accuracy Thunder and Dry Skin sustain. Skipping Klefki/Aegislash since their team lacks the slow bulky setup Klefki punishes and Hydreigon covers the Gengar matchup more offensively.
Raichu outspeeds and guarantees the Pelipper KO with Thunderbolt, while Primarina guarantees the Hydreigon KO with Moonblast.

Both foes have guaranteed OHKOs: Raichu Thunderbolt 4x kills Pelipper, Primarina Moonblast 4x kills Hydreigon, and Hydreigon can't meaningfully damage Primarina (all 0.5x or immune). Hydreigon must leave; Swampert switches in, takes neutral Moonblast easily, and next turn Mega Evolves to outspeed everything at 224 Speed in rain while threatening Earthquake (2x on Raichu, neutral on Primarina, Pelipper immune as Flying). Pelipper Protects to scout/waste Fake Out or Thunderbolt. Raichu's Lightning Rod also means Heliolisk can't Thunder Primarina until Raichu is gone, so breaking its sash with Swampert is the priority.
Thunderbolt guarantees the Pelipper KO, while Energy Ball guarantees Swampert is finished from 36%, strongly pressuring both Protect and Mega Evolution lines.

selection: Earthquake (all adjacent, including ally Pelipper) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Mega Swampert's rain-boosted Swift Swim Speed (224) outspeeds Raichu, and STAB Earthquake breaks Raichu's Focus Sash while chunking Primarina neutrally; Pelipper is Flying and immune to EQ. Pelipper pivots out before Raichu's 4x Thunderbolt lands, and Heliolisk resists Electric (0.5x) while becoming my rain-Thunder answer to Primarina next turn (Raichu at 1 HP can then be picked off by Swampert Waterfall).

Both actives fainted, so my only two remaining Pokémon must enter: Hydreigon in slot 1, Pelipper in slot 2. Rain is up for 7 more turns (Damp Rock). Raichu is at 1% with sash broken — any hit removes it and its Lightning Rod. Primarina (66%, Sitrus consumed) is the main threat: Hydreigon is 4x weak to Moonblast and cannot meaningfully hurt Primarina, so Pelipper's rain-boosted-accuracy Hurricane (23-40.6% per hit, 2HKO range) is my win condition into it. Slot order is cosmetic for targeting; Hydreigon slot a, Pelipper slot b. Next turn lean: Pelipper Wide Guard to block Liquid Voice Hyper Voice (Water-type spread, rain-boosted) while Hydreigon Dark Pulse removes Raichu; if Primarina shows Moonblast patterns instead, Hydreigon Protects while Pelipper Hurricanes.
Thunderbolt and Moonblast each guarantee an OHKO on their respective targets; Hydreigon cannot KO Primarina first.
Bring Gengar for its faster, accurate single-target pressure alongside Primarina against the lone Pelipper.

Hydreigon must Protect vs Moonblast, but only Pelipper can Protect this turn — instead, Heat Wave guarantees value: it KOs 1% Raichu on any hit (no Fake Out risk since Raichu has been out since T1) and chips Primarina so that a later Heat Wave + Hurricane combo enters KO range. Pelipper Protects because Raichu (143-178 Spe) outruns Pelipper and Thunderbolt is a guaranteed 4x OHKO; Pelipper attacking means dying before moving if Raichu targets it. This preserves Pelipper into next turn, guarantees Raichu's Lightning Rod is removed, and if Primarina wastes Moonblast into Pelipper's Protect, Hydreigon survives at full HP. Attacking Primarina directly cannot KO this turn (max ~48%) and leaves Hydreigon eating a 4x Moonblast with nothing gained.
Mega Shadow Ball plus Moonblast maximizes single-target damage through Wide Guard and should secure the final KO.

Hydreigon is fainted so slot 1 must pass. The game is effectively lost (Pelipper alone vs Gengar + Primarina + one unrevealed), so I play for maximum information and damage rather than conceding: Shadow Ball does not OHKO Pelipper (41-60%), so Pelipper likely survives a solo hit and can act. Hurricane into Gengar deals 34-67%, the biggest available chunk, and their response reveals Gengar's habits (Protect? Mega? Perish Song?) for games 2-3. Wide Guard only blocks their spread moves and gains nothing toward winning; Tailwind is useless with no partner.

reflections.summary: Team preview was well suited: Raichu and Primarina were the right lead, Tsareena provided useful priority insurance, and Mega Gengar was an appropriate cleaner even though Primarina did most of the work. Piloting cleanly exploited Primarina’s coverage to remove Mega Swampert and Hydreigon, while the opponent’s Earthquake also eliminated their own Heliolisk.
reflections.adjustment: If the Pelipper/Hydreigon lead repeats, anticipate Pelipper protecting and use Fake Out plus Moonblast into the Hydreigon slot, punishing either Hydreigon or a Swampert switch; then finish Swampert with Energy Ball.

reflections.summary: Lost by turn 2's catastrophic double-down: Mega Swampert's Earthquake KO'd my own Heliolisk (Ground-weak, Dry Skin doesn't help) while Swampert itself died to Primarina's targeted Energy Ball, leaving Hydreigon/Pelipper unable to break the Primarina+Gengar endgame. Compounded by turn 1 switching Swampert into a Moonblast that put it at 37% before it ever acted. Team-preview plan was defensible (rain engine vs their Shadow Tag core), but bringing Heliolisk into a Lightning Rod Raichu lead meant it contributed nothing before dying to friendly fire.
reflections.adjustment: Never click spread Ground moves with Heliolisk on the field — pair Swampert's EQ only with Pelipper (Flying-immune) or Protect the partner. Also stop switching Swampert into Primarina's Moonblast; preserve it at full HP so it survives Energy Ball range and can actually fire in rain, and remove Raichu before Heliolisk ever needs to attack.

Lead Pelipper + Hydreigon: rain on entry, Hydreigon resists Raichu's Electric attacks, is immune to Ground, and breaks Raichu's sash with Heat Wave while pressuring a potential early Gengar. Swampert stays healthy in back to Mega-sweep in rain once Raichu is chipped and Primarina is pressured; Heliolisk closes as the Primarina answer once Lightning Rod/sash are gone. Follows the game 2 plan exactly.
Fake Out plus Moonblast pressures Hydreigon while still covering a Swampert pivot into that slot.

Opponent habits are locked in: Raichu Thunderbolts the Pelipper slot (OHKO, always outruns) and Primarina 4x Moonblasts Hydreigon. Double Protect scouts both for free and also blanks a potential turn-1 Fake Out into Hydreigon. This preserves Pelipper as my rain setter and keeps Hydreigon healthy as my designated Gengar answer. Turn 2 I can Tailwind (or Hurricane Primarina) while Hydreigon breaks Raichu's Focus Sash with Draco Meteor, unlocking Heliolisk later. Switching Swampert in is off-limits into Primarina per plan, and Hydreigon attacking risks an immediate Moonblast OHKO.
Both attacks guarantee an OHKO if the foes stay in, while Moonblast still pressures a Swampert pivot into Hydreigon’s slot.

Hydreigon cannot stay in as Primarina's unprotected Moonblast target (OHKO), and Protect is success-reduced, so it pivots to Heliolisk — verified to survive Modest Moonblast (54.7-78.4%). Raichu's predictable Thunderbolt/Nuzzle into the Pelipper slot is completely walled by Swampert's Ground immunity, so Pelipper pivots there for free and stays alive in back to reset rain later. Resulting board: Swampert walls Raichu entirely (all its moves are Electric or used-up Fake Out), and once Raichu leaves or falls, Heliolisk (177 Spe) outruns and deletes Primarina with rain Thunder while Mega Swampert's rain Waterfall threatens Gengar. This preserves all four of my Pokémon with zero damage taken this turn.
Protect preserves Raichu and Lightning Rod through a likely Mega Swampert Earthquake while Primarina uses its strongest 4x-effective attack into Swampert.

selection: Earthquake (all adjacent, including ally Heliolisk) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Mega Swampert's Swift Swim makes it move before both foes in rain (no Fake Out available — Raichu already used its first-turn-out), guaranteeing Earthquake lands: it breaks Raichu's Focus Sash (83.8-174.8% from full) and chips Primarina 32-62%, while Heliolisk Protects to avoid friendly EQ and block any Moonblast/Thunderbolt aimed at it. Energy Ball is a confirmed guaranteed OHKO on Swampert, so this is a calculated gamble that Primarina repeats its observed Moonblast targeting (it has clicked Moonblast both turns, zero Energy Balls, and targeted Heliolisk's slot last turn); every conservative alternative burns Protects and rain turns while leaving the same EB exposure next turn, and Heliolisk's Electric moves are useless until Raichu faints due to Lightning Rod redirection. If Swampert survives, next turn Waterfall picks off 1-HP Raichu before it moves, freeing Heliolisk's Thunder to delete chipped Primarina.

Hydreigon switching in is too dangerous: Primarina's confirmed game-2 habit is Moonblasting the fresh switch-in slot, and Hydreigon is 4x weak to Fairy — that's a near-certain death, and I still need Hydreigon healthy as my late-game Mega Gengar answer. Pelipper takes neutral Moonblast comfortably and only dies if Raichu specifically fires Thunderbolt into slot 1 (Raichu can't Fake Out again). Pelipper also preserves Tailwind, Wide Guard for Liquid Voice Hyper Voice, and a rain reset. Once in, the plan is to break Raichu's Focus Sash (Weather Ball/Hurricane), remove Raichu so Heliolisk's rain-boosted Thunder unlocks, and keep Hydreigon protected in back for Gengar's late entry.

Thunderbolt guarantees the Pelipper KO if unprotected, while Moonblast finishes Heliolisk based on prior damage and also punishes a switch to Hydreigon. Lightning Rod protects Primarina from Heliolisk's Electric attacks.

Heliolisk cannot do meaningful work while Raichu's Lightning Rod redirects all Electric moves, so it uses Weather Ball (resisted but neutral vs Raichu in rain, ~40%) to break the Focus Sash; if Tbolt targets Heliolisk instead it survives on resistance plus Dry Skin recovery. Once Raichu's sash is broken and it falls to chip, Heliolisk's Thunder unlocks to clean Primarina, while Hydreigon stays benched as the Gengar answer.

Primarina's Moonblast is a guaranteed OHKO, while Protect preserves Raichu from Hydreigon's guaranteed KO into its current HP.

reflections.summary: Game 2 sealed the 2-0 because Raichu and Primarina matched up exceptionally well into the opponent’s rain four. Raichu pressured Pelipper and discouraged Heliolisk’s Electric attacks, while Primarina’s Energy Ball removed Mega Swampert and Moonblast handled Heliolisk and Hydreigon. The opponent’s Protect-heavy play and pivots preserved little offensive momentum, and the failed repeated Protects made the endgame straightforward. The Swampert critical hit removed meaningful uncertainty; the Heliolisk critical hit was likely unnecessary given the damage from the first Moonblast. The between-game Fake Out plus Moonblast adjustment was sound and did not backfire, although the opening double Protect denied its immediate payoff. Team preview was also good: Raichu and Primarina were the essential pair, Tsareena supplied secondary Swampert pressure, and Gengar offered a trap or clean option. Gengar never needed to enter or Mega Evolve, which was appropriate rather than a missed opportunity. Piloting was clean, including protecting Raichu from Earthquake and preserving the winning attackers. Energy Ball Primarina was the standout matchup-specific preparation; the available evidence does not show that Maushold, Diggersby, or any left-behind roster member would have produced a materially better four.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Raichu/Primarina lead and broadly the same four, with Tsareena prioritized as Swampert insurance and Mega Gengar treated as optional rather than an evolution that must be forced. Expect the opening double Protect and preserve Fake Out when that read is strong. After the demonstrated pivots, align Primarina’s Energy Ball with the Hydreigon-to-Swampert slot and Raichu’s Thunderbolt with the Pelipper slot instead of allowing Thunderbolt to meet Swampert. Continue preserving Primarina until Swampert and Hydreigon are resolved. No roster overhaul is justified from this series.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar leads with Intimidate+Fake Out to neuter physical attackers. Sylveon's spread Fairy damage threatens Dragonite, Garchomp, Whimsicott. Mega Metagross handles Garchomp/Ice Punch, Tinkaton, and Whimsicott. Dragapult outspeeds everything for cleanup and priority pressure.

Lead the standard Tailwind core: Prankster Tailwind flips the speed war against Dragapult/Meowscarada/Mega Metagross, while Sash guarantees it lands even through Fake Out; Garchomp spreads EQ damage into Metagross lines and pressures Incineroar/Sylveon. Bring Mega Dragonite as the one Mega — Multiscale secures a Dragon Dance and its Earthquake punishes Metagross, plus ESpeed cleans weakened foes. Tinkaton rounds out the four: it walls Pixilate Sylveon, threatens Dragapult/Meowscarada with Gigaton Hammer, provides Fake Out disruption and Thunder Wave insurance, and unlike Milotic it isn't setup bait for Meowscarada.

Fake Out Whimsicott to prevent Tailwind while Hyper Voice pressures both foes. Even if Whimsicott Protects, it wastes its turn. Garchomp's -1 Earthquake won't KO Incineroar, and Sitrus Berry provides recovery. Best turn 1 to seize momentum.

Their lead screams turn-1 Fake Out (Incineroar) plus Pixilate Hyper Voice, and that Hyper Voice computes to 83-124% into Garchomp — a possible OHKO if Garchomp exposes itself for only a 45-87% Iron Head back. Whimsicott's Protect blocks Fake Out entirely (no flinch), and even if Incineroar redirects Fake Out at Garchomp, a flinched Protect attempt still leaves Garchomp unharmed while Sylveon's spread move hits two Protects for nothing. Double Protect wastes their whole lead turn with zero risk, and since Incineroar can't reuse Fake Out next turn, turn 2 gives us a guaranteed safe Tailwind (Prankster) plus Garchomp attacking first into Sylveon at full HP.

Parting Shot on Garchomp lowers its Attack to -2 and SpA to -1, reducing its offensive threat, while switching Incineroar out to preserve momentum. Hyper Voice spreads Life Orb-boosted Pixilate Fairy damage to both foes, pressuring Garchomp (2x weak) and chipping Whimsicott's Focus Sash. Metagross or Dragapult comes in safely to handle the remaining threats.

Switching Incineroar to Metagross lets us Mega Evolve and KO Garchomp with Ice Punch (4x effective, 67-120% damage). Metagross easily survives any hit from -2 Atk Garchomp (Rock Slide 6-10%, Earthquake 40-56%) and Whimsicott's Moonblast is only 15-24% on Mega Metagross. This removes the biggest offensive threat while preserving Incineroar for later Intimidate pivoting.

Bring Dragapult for speed advantage (213) and Ground resistance. Double-target Garchomp with Ice Punch + Dragon Darts to secure the KO and remove the biggest spread threat. Dragapult outspeeds both foes and resists Earthquake, while Metagross can Mega Evolve for Tough Claws-boosted Ice Punch.

Double-target Garchomp for the KO. Ice Punch 4x + Mega Evolve Metagross for Tough Claws; Dragon Darts both hits on Garchomp since Whimsicott is Dragon-immune. Dragapult outspeeds both threats at 213. decisions.rationale: Incineroar provides Intimidate+Fake Out support and Parting Shot pivoting. Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice spreads heavy Fairy damage. Rotom-Wash covers Blaziken/Milotic with Water moves and burns physical threats. Metagross (Mega) brings Ice Punch for Garchomp/Dragonite and Meteor Mash for Tinkaton/Whimsicott.

Execute the g2 plan: Tinkaton+Whimsicott lead to Thunder Wave Metagross/Dragapult and burst Dragapult with Hammer+Helping Hand Moonblast; Garchomp answers Incineroar/Sylveon from the back; Milotic adds Icy Wind speed control, walls Incineroar's Flare Blitz, and its Competitive punishes Parting Shot's SpA drop. Leave Dragonite in reserve rather than feeding it to Intimidate stacks + Ice Punch.

Fake Out on Whimsicott to deny Tailwind (Incineroar's +3 priority outspeeds Prankster +1). Hyper Voice spreads damage: breaks Whimsicott's Focus Sash at 49.7-98.5% and chips Tinkaton at 16.1-28.1%. If Tinkaton Fake Outs Sylveon, both sides lose a turn—acceptable trade. If Tinkaton Fake Outs Incineroar, Sylveon still applies pressure. If Tinkaton attacks, Incineroar still flinches Whimsicott.

Tinkaton (114 Speed) beats Incineroar's 80-112 range, so my Fake Out resolves first and guarantees the flinch, denying Incineroar's Fake Out/Parting Shot this turn. Meanwhile Prankster Tailwind goes up immediately, letting Garchomp (148) outrun Dragapult/Meowscarada when it rotates in. Even if Sylveon's Hyper Voice pops Whimsicott's Focus Sash, the board state is favorable: no damage taken by Tinkaton, Tailwind active, and Incineroar's momentum stalled.

Flare Blitz KOs Whimsicott (guaranteed); Mystical Fire chips Tinkaton (super-effective); split targets hedge against Protect on either side. Even if Sylveon faints to Gigaton Hammer, removing Whimsicott and damaging Tinkaton is a favorable trade with Rotom-Wash and Mega Metagross in back.

Pass with Incineroar (will move later in the turn selection); switch Sylveon to Rotom-Wash which walls Tinkaton's remaining moves (Thunder Wave immunity, Gigaton Hammer locked, Fake Out unusable). Rotom-Wash threatens KO on low-HP Whimsicott with Thunderbolt or cripples Tinkaton with Will-o-Wisp. Metagross saved to handle dragon threats.

Whimsicott at 23% is guaranteed dead to any Sylveon spread/Fire hit, so it Protects to bank its second Tailwind cast for when this one expires. Tinkaton's Gigaton Hammer deals 51.5-102.4% to Sylveon (likely KO from 90%), while Helping Hand isn't worth sacrificing Whimsicott since even boosted rolls don't guarantee the OHKO across the legal bulk range.

Flare Blitz on Whimsicott guarantees the KO, removing Prankster Tailwind support. Will-O-Wisp on Tinkaton burns it, halving Gigaton Hammer's damage and adding chip, while Tinkaton's current attacks are already weak (7.6-19.3% range). This creates a favorable 2v1 position with a crippled Tinkaton remaining.

Whimsicott at 23% dies to any Flare Blitz and Protect may fail after last turn's use, so pivot it to Milotic, who resists every current threat (Flare Blitz/Hydro Pump/Thunderbolt) and keeps Competitive insurance vs Parting Shot. Tinkaton's Hammer is walled by both foes, so paralyze Rotom-Wash—their strongest staying special attacker—while Tailwind covers us.

Flare Blitz guarantees KO on burned Tinkaton (47% HP, 2x weakness). Will-O-Wisp cripples Garchomp's Attack. Even in worst case (Rock Slide 40-56% + Gigaton Hammer 6-9%), Sitrus Berry heals Incineroar to survive ~12-32% HP after Flare Blitz recoil. Removing Tinkaton's Mold Breaker now is critical.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Garchomp's Earthquake is a guaranteed KO on Incineroar (74.8-139.4%) even through Situs Berry, and we outspeed so Incineroar dies before it can Parting Shot or Flare Blitz. Tinkaton must Protect: it takes heavy EQ chip otherwise, Incineroar's Flare Blitz is a guaranteed KO on it, and preserving our Metagross wall matters more than its negligible 5-9% Hammer chip into Incineroar. Rotom's best follow-up (Hydro Pump on Garchomp) cannot KO from 75%.

Metagross Ice Punch guarantees KO on 65% Garchomp (4x effective). Mega Evolving for Tough Claws boost and likely Speed advantage. Rotom Hydro Pump targets Tinkaton (41% HP, burned) to clean up; if Garchomp Protects, at least Tinkaton takes chip damage. This avoids doubling into a potential Garchomp Protect and addresses both threats.

Mega Metagross (Jolly, likely max Speed ~178) outspeeds Garchomp 148 after evolving, and its Ice Punch is a guaranteed KO on Garchomp from 65% — so Garchomp must Protect this turn. Meanwhile Tinkaton paralyzes Metagross: afterward its Speed is ~36-45, so Garchomp outspeeds permanently and can spam Earthquake (64-112% spread, possible OHKO) safely next turn. Tailwind is unneeded — Garchomp already outruns Rotom (≤138) and un-Mega Metagross, and paralysis handles Mega.

Ice Punch guarantees Garchomp KO (4x effective, 93-164% on 65% HP). Hydro Pump is best chance to KO the burned 35% Tinkaton. If Garchomp Protects (reduced success rate), Rotom still threatens Tinkaton. Tinkaton cannot Fake Out (not its first turn) and Gigaton Hammer is negligible through resists+burn.

Tinkaton Protects so Garchomp's LO Earthquake safely spreads only onto paralyzed Mega Metagross (64-112%, possible OHKO; Rotom is Levitate-immune). Ally EQ would otherwise likely KO our burnt 36% Tinkaton, which is our best wall against Metagross. Even if Metagross survives, its paralysis means Garchomp always moves first for a follow-up EQ.

Garchomp is down, so bring in Milotic: it resists both of Rotom-Wash's STABs and Meteor Mash, so nothing on their side threatens it meaningfully, while Tinkaton (whose menu here limits it to passing) can next turn finish the 3% paralyzed Metagross with Gigaton Hammer and let Milotic stall out Rotom-Wash with Recover. Switching in 23% Whimsicott would just feed a likely Hydro Pump KO.

Protect Metagross-Mega to preserve it at 3% HP. Thunderbolt Milotic for super-effective damage; Tinkaton can't Fake Out again (used turn 1) and can't paralyze Electric-type Rotom, leaving Rotom free to act.

Burned -1 Tinkaton's Gigaton Hammer still guarantees the KO on the 3% paralyzed Metagross even through Steel resistance; Icy Wind chips Rotom-Wash (resisted but safe) and drops its Speed for the endgame while avoiding Surf recoil onto my own Tinkaton.

Rotom Thunderbolt guaranteed KOs Milotic at 47%. Metagross Meteor Mash guaranteed KOs Tinkaton at 23% if it survives to move, but Metagross is paralyzed and will likely faint first to any opposing attack. Either way, Rotom alone easily cleans up the burned 23% Tinkaton.

Icy Wind guarantees the KO on 3% Metagross (min rolls far exceed ~5 HP) even through its 0.5x Ice resistance, while Tinkaton Protects since Hammer isn't offered and Thunder Wave is redundant/immune; Milotic faces identical Rotom risk either way, so removing Metagross now leaves the favored Milotic-walls-Rotom endgame.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Metagross is fainted; only Pass is possible. Thunderbolt guarantees KO on Tinkaton (17%, guaranteed 26.6-47.5% range, 100% accuracy). Rotom survives any combined hit from Tinkaton's Gigaton Hammer (max 6.2%) and Whimsicott's Moonblast (max 41.4%) with ease, then finishes Whimsicott next turn.

Only path to victory is grinding Rotom-Wash with resisted Moonblast (21-39%/hit); Thunderbolt guarantees KO on 18% Tinkaton and everything else into Levitate Rotom fails (TWave immune, Hammer 0.25x, HH-crit Hammer only 10-19%), so chip with Hammer while Moonblast races the leftover-healing range — playing out keeps a nonzero win chance versus conceding at 0%.

Metagross-Mega is fainted, must Pass. Rotom-Wash uses Hydro Pump at Whimsicott (foe 2): it's a guaranteed KO if it connects (25.1-48.9% vs 23% HP). Rotom survives at least one Moonblast even if Hydro Pump misses, so the risk is acceptable. Thunderbolt is not guaranteed to KO, and Will-O-Wisp cannot KO. Winning this turn ends the game.

Only Whimsicott remains, so Tinkaton passes. Whimsicott outspeeds the paralyzed Rotom-Wash even at -2, so the only line that can ever win is immediate Moonblast pressure: chip Rotom now, and survive only if Rotom opts for Will-O-Wisp, Protects, or Hydro Pump misses (80%). Protecting concedes a free turn for zero benefit since we have no recovery and the Focus Sash is spent.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and series 2-0 due to strong team composition (Incineroar, Rotom-Wash, Mega Metagross, Sylveon) that countered the opponent's key threats. Rotom-Wash's bulk and typing allowed it to outlast after Tailwind expired. Critical KO on Garchomp via Metagross's Ice Punch (bypassing its Protect) and early burn on Tinkaton were decisive. Opponent's Protect-heavy strategy was managed effectively, and our team's synergy and type coverage proved superior.
reflections.adjustment: For a future rematch, consider replacing Incineroar with Skarmory to add a physical wall with Spikes pressure against Dragonite/Blaziken, or bring Dragapult for faster special offense. Swap Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump for Scald to improve accuracy and burn chance. Alternatively, include Meowscarada for priority and type advantage over Dragonite/Garchomp.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 because Rotom-Wash was again an unanswerable endgame piece. The midgame actually went well: Fake Out+Tailwind lead, Sylveon hammered down turn 2, a critical Earthquake removed Incineroar, and Thunder Wave crippled Mega Metagross before Icy Wind chip finished it. But every trade fed their win condition: Garchomp died to a predicted Ice Punch, Milotic was 2HKO'd by Thunderbolt despite leftovers, and the finale was burnt Tinkaton plus a sash-broken Whimsicott failing to out-damage Leftovers recovery — Gigaton Hammer resisted, Moonblast needing 3+ hits net of regen, Thunder Wave immune to Levitate. Between-game adjustments partially helped (the plan to answer Rotom early via paralysis and chip was correct in principle) but backfired in execution: the only Rotom 'answer' brought was Tinkaton, whose Hammer is resisted and who arrived burned. Team preview was mediocre: bringing Garchomp into a confirmed Ice Punch KO matchup traded tempo for one Incineroar kill, and neither registered Mega (Dragonite/Blaziken) was brought, so we fought their Mega Metagross with a Mega-less four.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, the draft must contain a true Rotom-Wash counter, not partial checks: a Grass-type special sponge (resists both Hydro Pump and Thunderbolt, ignores Will-O-Wisp relevance) or a Taunt/heavy-special-pressure piece that denies Leftovers stall. Bring one of our own Megas so we are not out-stat'ed by Mega Metagross — Mega Dragonite over Garchomp would keep the Earthquake-style pressure without losing to Ice Punch. Lead to preserve Whimsicott's Focus Sash: do not expose it to turn-1 Hyper Voice; either Protect-first with the partner or accept that Tailwind must come from a sash-safe position. Treat their Rotom as the series-deciding mon: commit two slots to answering it rather than one.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 because Trick Room never went up and opponent's core hard-counters it. Game2 preview doubled down on the same TR plan (Farigiraf Armor Tail + Hatterene Magic Bounce) but opponent led Mega Floette + Kingambit instead of expected Sinistcha. T1 Light of Ruin OHKO'd Hatterene (51% recoil) + Iron Head 50% + flinch on Farigiraf denied TR entirely - no Protect/redirect to play around flinch. Between-game adjustment backfired: you benched your best TR attackers (Mega Camerupt/Rhyperior) for Gholdengo/Araquanid to answer predicted Sinistcha lead with Helping Hand Shadow Ball/Wide Guard. vs Floette lead Gholdengo traded 1-for-1 (Make It Rain super-effective vs Floette but resisted vs Kingambit, then OHKO'd by Kowtow) leaving Farigiraf/Araquanid 2v2 into Sinistcha Imprison (locks TR) + Kingambit cleaner where Helping Hand Liquidation only left Kingambit at 22% before Matcha Gotcha + Kowtow crit closed. Prep 6/10: Farigiraf/Hatterene tech, Araquanid Wide Guard, and Rhyperior/Camerupt TR attackers were the right ideas vs Imprison, and Araquanid proved best Floette answer, but Hatterene Life Orb is too frail to Light of Ruin, Gholdengo set doesn't solve Kingambit, and leaving Rhyperior on bench Game2 removed your best Rock/Steel pressure into Floette. Full roster offered no material fix - Mega Chandelure/Reuniclus/Wyrdeer/Trevenant share same Kingambit Dark/Steel weakness and don't fix the T1 OHKO/flinch vs Floette; Rhyperior over Gholdengo was the only strictly better swap available.
reflections.adjustment: Future series vs same opponent: do not lead double passive setters vs Floette/Kingambit and do not rely on Hatterene to live Light of Ruin - give it Sash/bulk or swap to Reuniclus. Bring Rhyperior + Araquanid as the two TR sweepers, bench Gholdengo when Floette is expected (Make It Rain fails into Kingambit and loses to Kowtow) and only bring Camerupt-Mega if TR is guaranteed. Guarantee T1 TR with Farigiraf Protect + Hatterene TR (Mental Herb covers Taunt, Armor Tail covers Prankster only, not Iron Head flinch) or lead Farigiraf + attacker with Protect. Target Floette first with Rock/Steel (Rhyperior) not Kingambit, keep Wide Guard Araquanid for Moonblast/Matcha. Accept you must ignore Sinistcha Imprison T1 and just set TR rather than Helping Hand.

events.text: Stealth Rock up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Lead with Charizard slot 0 to mega-evolve into Charizard-Y, triggering Drought via speed-ordered mega evolution to override Hippowdon's Sand Stream and empower Fire STAB against the sand core and Fairy threats. Pair with Sneasler slot 1 as the second lead to leverage White Herb + Unburden under sun for explosive physical pressure. Bring Noivern slot 2 in the back for Tailwind speed control to outpace faster threats like Mega Delphox, and Corviknight slot 3 for Defog hazard removal and Light Screen support to withstand the opponent's special attackers (Delphox, Talonflame).

Sand core lead Hippowdon + Excadrill. Hippowdon sets Sand Stream, Excadrill outspeeds the opponent's whole team with Sand Rush (and even without sand, 154 Speed is fast). Back is Mega Delphox for special offense (Levitate avoids EQ, covers Noivern/Toxapex) and Talonflame for Gale Wings priority Brave Bird and Tailwind support. Drop Clefable (redundant tank) and Conkeldurr (too slow, weak to opponent's Flying-types, overlaps with Excadrill).

Mega Evolve Charizard (Drought replaces sandstorm, removes Excadrill's Sand Rush, drops Excadrill Speed from 236-308 to 118-154). This lets Sneasler (Spe 172) act first and Close Combat Excadrill for a guaranteed OHKO (111.5% min). Charizard then Flamethrowers Hippowdon with sun-boosted 232 SpA. Charizard is immune to Hippowdon's Earthquake (Ground immunity via Flying), so only Sneasler takes EQ damage. This eliminates the primary physical threat (Rock Slide 4x vs Charizard), establishes sun, and keeps both Pokemon alive.

Stealth Rock is essential against this team—Charizard-Y is 4x weak and Noivern/Corviknight are weak too. Excadrill's Rock Slide targets Charizard-Y for massive 4x SE damage (87-163% possible OHKO) and chips Sneasler. Sun WILL go up this turn regardless because Mega Evolution happens before moves, so preserving Excadrill's Sand Rush isn't possible. Best to maximize immediate damage and set up long-term hazards. Sneasler will likely CC Excadrill (guaranteed OHKO) to trigger Unburden, but Rock Slide output is the best use of Excadrill's last stand. Earthquake from Hippowdon only hits Sneasler for modest chip; Stealth Rock's value across the matchup is far higher.

Hippowdon must Pass (forfeit is unacceptable). Bringing in Talonflame is better than Delphox here: Gale Wings gives Brave Bird priority to bypass Sneasler's Unburden-boosted 280-344 Speed, Flare Blitz hits hard in sun, Sharp Beak boosts Flying damage, and Tailwind offers team-wide speed control (doubling Talonflame to 356 Speed, outspeeding Sneasler). Delphox would need a turn to Mega Evolve before attacking, and Sneasler likely OHKOs either switch-in regardless, so the priority option gives the best chance to deal damage first.

Charizard Flamethrower (sun-boosted, 60.5-113.1%) guaranteed KOs Hippowdon at 18% before it can act (Charizard 152 Speed > Hippowdon 67-99). Sneasler switches to Corviknight to evade Gale Wings Brave Bird OHKO (142.7-222.9%), preserving the Unburden-boosted Sneasler for late-game while bringing in a tank that quad-resists Brave Bird (12.7-20% damage) and can Defog our side's Stealth Rock next turn.

Hippowdon at 19% HP is dead weight in Sun (Sand Stream overridden, can't act safely). Switching to Delphox triggers Mega Evolution (Levitate, 159 SpA) for an immediate major special threat. Talonflame's Gale Wings priority Brave Bird (2x SE on Fighting) into Sneasler removes the dangerous Unburden-boosted threat before it can attack. Charizard's sun-boosted Flamethrower hits Delphox (0.5x Fire resist) for limited damage. This play removes Sneasler, preserves Hippo on the bench (to re-enter later when Sun ends and Sand returns), and keeps Talonflame at full HP so Gale Wings priority is intact for next turn.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Charizard-Mega-Y)
decisions.rationale: Charizard Flamethrower -> Delphox (32-58% damage, only target with achievable KO at 50% HP; Talonflame attack can't KO at 92%). Corviknight Light Screen is mandatory: Heat Wave is a guaranteed OHKO without it (74-106% vs 71% HP), but Light Screen (8 turns w/ Light Clay) halves it to 37-53%, keeping Corviknight alive to Defog next turn. Preserves both Pokémon and the sun-boosted win condition through remaining weather turns.

Both Charizard and Corviknight fainted. Must bring out both remaining Pokémon (Sneasler + Noivern). Gale Wings is inactive on Talonflame (69% HP, not full), so Sneasler's 344 Speed outspeeds everything on Turn 5 — it can strike first with Dire Claw (40-78% vs Delphox at 50%, 40-77% vs Talonflame at 69%) before Talonflame can Brave Bird. Placing Noivern in Slot 1 (Charizard's former slot, primary target on Turns 2-3) has a reasonable chance of drawing single-target attacks that Noivern can survive better (resists Flying 0.5x). Sneasler in Slot 2 may evade targeting and survive Turn 4's spread moves. Even if Sneasler falls, Noivern (Hurricane: 59-114% vs Talonflame at 69%) can eliminate Talonflame, then face a weakened Hippowdon (18% HP, takes Stealth Rock on entry, Noivern immune to its Earthquake). Forfeiting yields 0% win probability; playing offers multiple viable KO paths.

Mega Evolve Delphox to outspeed Charizard-Y with higher SpA/SpD. Heat Wave (spread) is a guaranteed KO on Corviknight at 70% HP (2x SE Fire) and chips Charizard-Y for 16-29%. Talonflame's Brave Bird into Charizard-Y at 50-94% damage combined with Heat Wave chip has high OHKO upside. Even if Charizard-Y survives, it's left at 0-50% HP and basically dead. The double attack into Corviknight via Heat Wave is overkill but ensures Corviknight dies (denying Defog of my Stealth Rock). With Mega Delphox's boosted SpD, Charizard-Y's Flamethrower counter does less than 41-57% into my Delphox, making the trade favorable.

Sneasler Dire Claw -> Delphox-Mega (40-78% vs 50% HP, ~74% KO chance, 30% status chance, no stat drops) targets first and fastest. Noivern Draco Meteor -> Talonflame (70-135% vs 69% HP) guarantees KO of the 2x SE Brave Bird threat. If Sneasler KOs Delphox-Mega (74%), both foes eliminated for game win. If Sneasler misses (26%), Delphox-Mega Psychics Sneasler (guaranteed OHKO at 232-324%), but Noivern still removes Talonflame, leaving a severely weakened Delphox-Mega for cleanup next turn. Both foes' SE moves OHKO Sneasler regardless, so maximizing threat elimination is paramount.

Talonflame's priority Brave Bird (Gale Wings +1) guarantees a KO on Sneasler before it can attack, denying Sneasler's Close Combat setup for Noivern's cleanup. Delphox targets Noivern with Psychic (42-79% damage, ~12% KO chance) so its move isn't wasted when Sneasler faints first. Talonflame takes 33% recoil (47-94% of max HP), but has ~55-76% survival odds, leaving me 2v1 vs a damaged or KO'd Noivern in the best case. Protecting with Talonflame would let Sneasler attack Delphox, dropping it to 26-36% HP and letting Noivern's Draco Meteor KO it next turn, which is worse than the recoil risk.

reflections.summary: Lost because the opponent's core outsped and outtraded ours. We sent in Charizard-Mega-Y (Flamethrower) into a Sun-boosted Delphox-Mega that was faster (Timid) and survived our hit to OHKO back with Heat Wave, while our Noivern/Sneasler couldn't cleanly answer a faster Delphox and a GaleWings Talonflame. The matchup plan (Charizard + Noivern speed cores) had no hard answer to Delphox's speed tier or Tailwind from Talonflame, and once Charizard fell, we lacked the damage to answer both foes before their Brave Birds/Draco Meteor cleaned up. Effectively we committed to a sun strategy that let Delphox set up Mega and pressure our Charizard before our speed control could engage.
reflections.adjustment: Bring a faster or priority answer to the opponent's core: consider leading with Sneasler + Corviknight (Defog + Light Screen) to survive entry and buy a turn, and save Charizard for after a Tailwind from Noivern rather than committing it early into a known faster special attacker. Also, avoid letting Noivern take a Psychic on turn 4 with such low HP; instead, bring in a Fairy/Steel or faster revenge killer so we can remove Delphox or Talonflame cleanly before they break our team.

reflections.summary: Won by pivoting cleanly after losing Excadrill to Sneasler's Close Combat on turn 1. Mega Delphox Heat Wave crit KO'd Corviknight turn 3, Talonflame Gale Wings Brave Bird KO'd Charizard and later Sneasler, and Hippowdon's Stealth Rock + Noivern's Life Orb recoil finished Noivern at 8% HP turn 4. Mega Delphox was the right Mega to bring (Levitate dodges Earthquake, spreads around Corviknight/Noivern/Charizard with STAB Heat Wave + Psychic) and the Talonflame pairing punished the opponent's frail offensive core.
reflections.adjustment: Do not lead Excadrill against a Sneasler+Charizard opener again — Sneasler's Adamant Close Combat OHKOs Excadrill before Sand Rush can matter, and Charizard's Drought overrides Sand Stream anyway, gutting the sand-sweep plan. Lead Hippowdon + Talonflame (or Hippowdon + Conkeldurr) so Talonflame can revenge Sneasler with priority Brave Bird and avoid losing the speed war, then bring Excadrill only if sand is actually up.

decisions.rationale: Lead Noivern for Tailwind speed control, Corviknight for pivot/utility, Toxapex as defensive backbone, Sneasler as late-game win condition. Avoids Charizard into sun/Delphox matchups.

Lead Mega Delphox + Talonflame to handle the likely Sneasler + Mega Charizard-Y lead: Mega Delphox Heat Wave spreads in sun and Levitate pivots around Ground moves; Talonflame's Gale Wings Brave Bird KOs Sneasler on the priority slot. Back Hippowdon for Stealth Rock + Slack Off sustain (notebook: SR chip on this squad is decisive — chunked Noivern to 0 in game 1), Clefable for Follow Me redirection to protect Delphox from Charizard-Y Hurricane and Noivern Draco Meteor, plus ThunderWave speed control and Moonblast (2x SE on Sneasler). Avoiding Excadrill (Sneasler CC trap, sand denied by Drought) and benching Conkeldurr this game in favor of Clefable's defensive utility.
