decisions.rationale: No rationale supplied.
No rationale supplied.

Mega Evolve Delphox for the +45 SpA boost and Levitate (Ground immunity for future pivots). Heat Wave hits both foes, dealing massive 2x SE damage to Corviknight and chipping Noivern. Talonflame Brave Bird with Gale Wings +1 priority outspeeds Noivern's STAB priority-0 moves and lands neutral Flying damage before Noivern can Draco/Tailwind. Goal: pressure the immediate offensive threat (Noivern) while chunking the bulkier pivot (Corviknight) to set up future KOs, and lock in Mega Delphox's Levitate for the rest of the game.

Close Combat on Delphox-Mega guarantees Unburden activation via White Herb consumption (stat drops trigger even through Protect), doubling Sneasler's Speed to 344 if it survives. This is the only move that can flip the speed disadvantage — at 344 Speed, Sneasler outspeeds all opposing Pokémon and can clean up with Dire Claw next turn. If Sneasler falls, Close Combat still deals 30-58% damage to the primary win condition. Corviknight (14% HP) must switch to Toxapex to avoid certain OHKO from Heat Wave, bringing in a bulky wall that resists Fire (0.25x) and Flying (0.25x) while positioning Sneasler to survive and capitalize on the Unburden speed boost.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sneasler with White Herb + Unburden is the biggest threat — if it uses Close Combat this turn, White Herb cures the drops and Unburden activates, doubling its Speed next turn to potentially outspeed my whole team. I need to OHKO it before that happens. Talonflame's Brave Bird with Gale Wings priority + 2x SE Flying into Fighting/Poison guarantees an OHKO (113-226% range) and hits before Sneasler can move. Delphox-Mega's Heat Wave (spread, both foes) KOs Corviknight at 14% even through Light Screen (39-74% range), and if Corviknight switches out, the spread still chips whatever comes in. This double-removes both opposing threats this turn with no recoil to my team. Avoid Tailwind this turn — Sneasler must die first.

Both opponent Pokémon outspeed Corviknight (146-204 vs 87) and guarantee an OHKO with Fire-type moves at Corviknight's 14% HP, making Corviknight's move likely lost. Brave Bird → Talonflame (index 4) maximizes damage output with a possible KO at 50% HP (31.4-62.7% range), superior to Brave Bird vs Delphox (no KO possible at 100%) and U-turn (70 BP, lower damage). Toxic Spikes (index 1) is the key play: it establishes long-term residual damage against all opponent switch-ins, particularly devastating against Sand/Rush cores (Hippowdon/Excadrill) where Toxic + Sand damage stacks, and it weakens late-game threats. Toxapext can safely absorb Heat Wave (9-13% through Light Screen + 0.5x resistance) while setting up, and faces significantly reduced threat with Talonflame potentially eliminated, removing the Gale Wings priority user (already inactive at 50% HP).

Flare Blitz is a guaranteed OHKO on Corviknight at 14% (Fire STAB + 2x SE on Steel, Sharp Beak boost, Corviknight has no recovery and is locked in since Charizard/Stunfisk weren't brought). Delphox-Mega Psychic on Toxapex does 48-84% (2x SE Psychic vs Poison), forcing it to Recover and denying a free pivot — spreading Heat Wave would be wasted since Corviknight dies to Talonflame anyway and Toxapex resists Fire. Speed order (Delphox 204 > Talonflame 178 > Corviknight 87-119) means both KOs land before Corviknight can act. After this turn the opponent is down to a chipped Toxapex with no good switch-ins to my team.

Toxapex at 50% is OHKO'd by Delphox Psychic alone (48.4-66.2%). Baneful Bunker (priority +4) acts first, blocking all attacks this turn with 100% guarantee vs ~50% survival from Recover-at-100% HP. Talonflame's Brave Bird/Flare Blitz make contact -> poisoned (-12.5%/turn). Next turn: Recover to 100% with Light Screen still active, then face double attack (~50% survival) — overall 2-turn survival probability 50% vs 25% for Recover-now. Toxic Spikes already on foe field for switch-ins. Corviknight fainted -> Pass.

Both active Pokemon outspeed Toxapex (55-87) and any Charizard-Y switch-in (120-152). Toxapex is at 49% and is the immediate target — Delphox Psychic (SE 2x, 48-84%) and Talonflame Brave Bird (34-60%) together give high odds to KO. Even if opponent switches Charizard-Y into slot a, both moves still target Toxapex in slot b. If Toxapex uses Baneful Bunker, Delphox's Psychic is special and bypasses the block. Removing Toxapex collapses their defensive pivot and the Toxic Spikes setter, leaving only Charizard-Y (must still Mega Evolve next turn) and Stunfisk-Galar — both weak to Fire moves from Delphox/Talonflame. Protecting Talonflame would waste a precious damage turn while it's being chipped by Toxic Spikes poison; attacking maximizes the chance to eliminate their wall before Charizard-Y comes online.

decisions.rationale: Corviknight is fainted (0% HP) and can only Pass; forfeiting would concede the series. Toxipex MUST use Baneful Bunker (+4 priority) because both faster foes (Delphox 169-204, Talonflame 146-178) will attack the only remaining target. Combined Psychic (48.4-66.2%) + Brave Bird (26.8-40.8%) = 75.2-107% guaranteed OHKO from Toxipex's 55% HP. Without priority (Recover, Venoshock, Toxic Spikes), Toxipex is defeated before acting — 0% survival. Baneful Bunker's +4 priority moves first, blocking both attacks with 50% success. Even 50% survival odds > 0%. If Baneful Bunker lands, Toxipex remains at 55% HP, Talonflame (already poisoned at 32%) faces additional residual damage, and Toxic Spikes is pre-deployed on foe side for incoming switches.

Toxapex at 55% is the only foe and the lone obstacle to sweeping the back. Double-target it for max KO odds. Delphox Psychic hits 48-84% (roll-to-KO range) while Light Screen is up. Talonflame Brave Bird hits 34-60% on Toxapex (neutral, Sharp Beak boosted) with the side benefit of pressuring if Toxapex goes Recover. Talonflame is at 32% psn and will likely faint regardless, so trading it for a chance to break Toxapex is correct. Tailwind is unnecessary since Delphox already outspeeds Charizard-Y/Stunfisk. Shadow Ball/Heat Wave are NVE or weak against Toxapex and can't KO from 55%.

reflections.summary: The series was lost because the team was structurally outmatched by the opponent's offensive framework. Delphox-Mega provided immediate offensive pressure (turn 1 Heat Wave KOing Noivern through Light Screen) while Talonflame and priority users (Conkeldurr, Excadrill) punished any setup attempts. Sneasler's White Herb + Unburden setup was eliminated turn 2 by Talonflame's priority Brave Bird at 57% HP, removing the primary offensive threat before it could act. The defensive backbone (Corviknight, Toxapex) could not generate meaningful offense and folded quickly under repeated super-effective special attacks. Turn 3 saw Corviknight OHKOed by Flare Blitz after setting Light Screen, and Toxapex was overwhelmed by Psychic pressure without any real counterplay. The team lacked speed control, priority denial, and a viable win condition against a Sand-core offensive team that could punish every switch-in with super-effective coverage and priority.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a future series, register Venusaur and Swampert and lead with priority answers. Venusaur's Rage Powder + Sleep Powder can slow Delphox-Mega and enable setup for teammates, while Swampert provides a Water/Ground pivot that resists Fire/Flying and can set Stealth Rock. Replace Corviknight with a faster Defogger (Pelipper for Driogate + U-turn) or keep Corviknight but pair it with a priority blocker like Tsareena (Queenly Majesty) to shut down Talonflame and Conkeldurr. Mega Charizard Y needs Focus Sash or a faster mode to survive turn 1 Heat Wave, or pivot to a more defensive Charizard set to wall Physical Dragon/Fairy. The core issue was giving up too much tempo early – bring faster priority users who can win the speed battle before the opponent sets up Sand.

reflections.summary: Series won 2-0. Game 2 was a clean 5-turn blowout built entirely on the Talonflame + Mega Delphox core. The opponent's predicted Sneasler + Mega Charizard Y lead never materialized; instead they led Noivern + Corviknight, and Talonflame's Brave Bird + Delphox-Mega's Heat Wave punished that lead immediately (Noivern fainted turn 1, Sneasler fainted turn 2, Corviknight fainted turn 3). The only obstacle was Toxapex with Baneful Bunker, which stalled turns 4-5 until Baneful Bunker eventually failed and Delphox's Psychic finished it. The team-preview read was wrong on the lead but right on the core: Mega Delphox + Talonflame is the engine against this squad regardless of which two they open with. Hippowdon and Clefable never entered the game — both were bench warmers. Between-game adjustments from game 1 (keeping Mega Delphox, pairing it with Talonflame) were decisive.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Talonflame + Mega Delphox pairing as the locked-in core for any future series. Bring Clefable as the fourth for Follow Me redirection against predicted Hurricane/Draco Meteor from Noivern or Charizard-Y, and consider swapping Hippowdon for Conkeldurr if you want more Sneasler insurance — Excadrill is dead weight unless Charizard-Y is actually on the field. If you read the lead as Noivern + Corviknight (or anything not setting Drought), lead Delphox + Talonflame and click Heat Wave + Brave Bird into the pair — the spread pressure is backbreaking. Save Hippowdon for the Charizard-Y gameplan (sand vs Drought weather war + Stealth Rock) rather than bringing it when their sun team isn't deployed.
